purpose: Canonical interpretation of owner-camera evidence for Jubilee sensing. Owner-authorized private media may follow existing publication/archive policy; this contract governs model meaning and detectability.

view_geometry.primary_view: waterline where Mobile Bay water reaches the sand at 437 Village
view_geometry.lateral_extent: 437 beach plus neighboring beach segments immediately north and south
view_geometry.fixed_biological_reference: old cedar stumps standing in shallow water
view_geometry.regional_context: 437 lies on a mostly accessible sandy shoreline extending roughly 1 mile north toward May Day and more than 2 miles south toward Fly Creek Marina; the camera itself does not directly observe that full corridor

high_value_signals: crabs climbing cedar stumps or leaving water
fish shrimp eels rays or other marine life crowding the swash zone
unusual concentrated surface activity at the shoreline
predawn anonymous people walking the beach with lights and looking at the water
dawn anonymous people using nets gigs buckets or sustained search behavior
clustered or slow focused human search behavior
nearshore water smoothness chop or localized disturbance
unusual bird concentration close to the shoreline

timing_interpretation.full_darkness: Owner-supplied night image confirms the shoreline scene is generally too dark for reliable biological negatives or fine waterline interpretation. Bright moving lights or illuminated people may still be detectable, but absence of such evidence is not a Jubilee negative.
timing_interpretation.predawn: Human lights/search behavior is a high-information soft precursor because ordinary predawn beach foot traffic is uncommon at this low-public-access shoreline. Biological interpretation remains gated by measured scene illumination/visibility.
timing_interpretation.first_light_and_daylight: Increase emphasis on direct shoreline biology, especially cedar-stump crab activity, stranded/crowded marine life, swash-zone aggregation and visible searching with nets or gigs. Owner expects these features to be visible once there is natural light.

visibility_gate.dark_scene: UNKNOWN for biology and shoreline-negative inference
visibility_gate.light_source_detection: allowed as soft human-search evidence when clearly visible
visibility_gate.first_light_transition: begin principal biological assessment only when the waterline and cedar-stump reference area are visibly resolved
visibility_gate.daylight: full shoreline biology/search interpretation permitted subject to freshness and obstruction checks

cameras.negative_scope: When the capture is fresh, unobstructed and sufficiently illuminated, absence of shoreline biological activity or unusual search behavior is meaningful only for the beach segments actually visible in the frame and observation interval. It is not a negative for all Montrose, May Day, Fly Creek, Fairhope or Point Clear.
cameras.human_privacy: Count and classify anonymous behavior only. No identity recognition and no cross-camera person tracking.

cameras.view_geometry: Primarily water roughly 150+ feet offshore; water remains shallow, approximately 3 feet deep or less at the pier end.
allowed_signals: anonymous visible human activity when present
cameras.guardrail: Supporting shallow-water evidence, not a substitute for the shoreline-contact view from montrose_shoreline.

cameras.look_direction_owner_confirmed: approximately due west over Mobile Bay
cameras.shoreline_visible: not a direct beach close-up; marina/nearby structures and a distant/partial shoreline cue may be visible
cameras.view_geometry: From the Point Clear site, looks essentially due west over Mobile Bay. The view includes the marina axis/nearby structures and broad Bay water; any shoreline cue is distant and secondary rather than a close swash-zone view.
high_value_signals: anonymous people or lights moving along marina/shoreline axis when resolvable
clustered human activity near any resolvable distant shoreline patch
localized surface disturbance or fish activity within marina or adjacent Bay
broad due-west Bay surface-state and visibility context
visible biological concentration near distant shoreline only when image resolution is sufficient
cameras.negative_scope: Absence of visible activity is only evidence for the resolvable marina/Bay corridor and any distant shoreline patch actually visible during the observed interval. Do not treat it as a negative for Point Clear beaches outside the frame.
cameras.mapping_guardrail: Do not hard-code camera-specific automation against pcl_e2_bay_mouth until the desktop/runtime display label 'Down the Marina' is explicitly mapped to this camera ID; owner currently believes this is the matching ID.

site_independence_rules: All three Montrose owner cameras share the montrose_owner_cluster physical/site independence group; multiple views improve observability but do not count as three independent Jubilee confirmations.

missingness_rule: Dark, stale, frozen, obstructed or otherwise inadequate views are UNKNOWN, not negatives.
